title: GPU reserve matrix and KV compactification playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Define and implement a practical GPU 'reserve matrix' that splits device memory into stable weight residency, a compacted/elastic KV region, and an activation headroom corridor; augment continuous-batching runtime with a lightweight KV compactification path to reduce fragmentation and improve burst headroom without blocking critical inference.

Background: We see recurring tail latency and OOM close-calls during tenant microbursts despite existing soft-watermarks and slabbed allocation. Analysis shows: (1) KV growth from long-lived chat sessions plus token-heavy prompts increases resident KV footprint over time; (2) activation bursts transiently need headroom but are denied due to weight/kv fragmentation; (3) full eviction strategies are too disruptive for low-latency SLOs. This ticket consolidates a pragmatic set of changes: a Reserve Matrix policy, a background KV compactifier, improved admission control for continuous batching, and telemetry to validate safety and cost trade-offs.

Scope (MVP):
- Define Reserve Matrix config and default values per GPU class (A100-80G, H100-80G, 4090/4090Ti) as device profiles.
- Implement a non-blocking KV compactification routine that: scans per-tenant KV segments, consolidates small unused slots, and coalesces free spans into a headroom pool; compaction intentionally yields to inference if latency budget is tight.
- Add admission control bloom-check that rejects/queues new continuous batches when projected headroom < threshold.
- Provide a runtime knob 'reserve_matrix.mode' with values: strict | adaptive | permissive.
- Add end-to-end telemetry (per-tenant kv_bytes, compacted_bytes, headroom_pct, batch_queue_latency) and dashboard.

Non-goals: full offline GC of KV to disk, wholesale weight offloading, or changes to model kernel selection in this ticket.

Success metrics (MVP):
- Reduction in OOM close-calls by >= 70% for observed microbursts in staging load test.
- 30-60% reduction in mean KV fragmentation bytes per GPU after 24h for long-lived sessions.
- No increase in p95 latency > 5% compared to baseline when reserve_matrix.mode=adaptive.

Trade-offs and design notes:
- Compaction vs latency: compaction must be preemptible and operate incrementally to avoid blocking the critical path. We prefer small incremental moves (< 1MB chunks) and yielding between batches.
- Memory accounting complexity: we choose simple per-tenant segment metadata (head, tail, free_list) to keep CPU overhead low; future follow-ups can add probabilistic estimation to reduce metadata size.
- Conservative defaults: adaptive mode will target 12-15% headroom for interactive tiers and 6-8% for batch-only tiers.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design: Reserve matrix schema and device profile table (runtime-config) + compaction algorithm spec. (Owner: Marco)
2) Telemetry: Add counters/gauges and a staging Grafana dashboard. (Owner: Priya Gupta)
3) Runtime: implement compactifier worker, admission check, and config knobs. (Owner: Marco)
4) E2E test: create synthetic long-lived-chat load harness to validate compaction and headroom. (Owner: Eng QA)

Write compaction algorithm: incremental scan + slot coalescing with yield points
Implement compactifier worker and lifecycle hooks in runtime
Add runtime knob reserve_matrix.mode and per-tenant config override
Admission control hook for continuous batching path
Instrument telemetry: kv_fragmentation_bytes, kv_compacted_bytes, headroom_percent, admission_denies
Create Grafana dashboard and SLO alerts for increased admission_denies or rising fragmentation
Load test harness for long-lived chat and microburst scenarios
Document operational playbook and rollback plan
acceptance_criteria: Reserve matrix config committed and validated on staging cluster
Compactifier runs without increasing p95 latency beyond 5% in adaptive mode
Telemetry dashboard shows expected compaction activity and headroom recovery under simulated load
No customer-facing errors or OOMs introduced by rollout in 2-canary nodes
